# pcfg: ported to Alea.jl from PluckArtifact.jl/src/table1/sequence_models/
# pluck/pcfg.jl of the artifact of Bowers et al., "Stochastic Lazy
# Knowledge Compilation for Inference in Discrete Probabilistic Programs"
# (PLDI 2025), Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.15051140 (CC-BY-4.0): the Pluck
# program of the paper's Table 1, row PCFG. The query is the probability
# that the grammar
#   S  -> XX YY | YY XX     (by a flip 0.5)
#   XX -> a | b XX XX       (a by a flip 0.5)
#   YY -> c | c XX | c S    (c alone by a flip 0.5, then XX or S by another)
# generates TARGET from S. The artifact's Dice.jl baseline
# (sequence_models/dice/pcfg.jl) is another grammar (YY -> c XX by 0.5)
# and bounds its recursion by fuel; this port is Pluck's grammar, bounded
# by the target alone.
#
# The generation reads the target left to right: generates(sym, i, j)
# is that sym, generated at position i, is the target's symbols i to
# j - 1. Each choice is keyed by its symbol and its position, which gives
# the original's distribution where no derivation expands one symbol twice

# sequence_models/pluck/string_editing.jl of the artifact of Bowers et al.,
# "Stochastic Lazy Knowledge Compilation for Inference in Discrete

# (CC-BY-4.0): the Pluck program of the paper's Table 1, row String
# Editing, with the perturb its benchmark defines (perturb_defs, "the one
# we're using"). The query is the probability that perturb turns INPUT
# into OUTPUT:
#   perturb Nil         = random_string 0.99
#   perturb (Cons c cs) = let delete = flip 0.01, insertion = random_string 0.99,
#                             rest = perturb cs
#                         in if delete then rest
#                            else insertion ++ Cons (if flip 0.01 then random_char else c) rest
#   random_string p     = if flip p then Nil else Cons random_char (random_string p)
# with random_char uniform over a to e. The artifact's Dice.jl baseline
# (sequence_models/dice/string_editing.jl) is another model and bounds
# its recursion by fuel; this port is Pluck's model, bounded by the two
# strings alone.
#
# The perturbation is read against OUTPUT left to right: perturbs(k, i)
# is that perturb of INPUT from position k is OUTPUT from position i to
# its end, and inserts(k, i, j) that the string inserted before input
# position k (k = length(INPUT) + 1: after the input) is OUTPUT's
# characters i to j - 1. A choice is keyed by the input position it
# perturbs and, within an inserted string, by the output position it
# writes, which gives the original's distribution where no perturbation
# reads one key twice. The input positions are perturbed once each, in
# order, and an inserted string writes each output position once, its end
# read at the position after its last character; an empty insertion, or a
# deleted input character, leaves the output position to the next input
# position, a key of its own. No perturbation then reads one key twice, it
# has the original's probability, and the choices at its keys fix it, so
# that two perturbations exclude each other.
using Alea

const QUERY = :pr

const INPUT = "edcc"
const OUTPUT = "eddde"

function string_editing_perturbs(input, output)
    n, m = length(input), length(output)
    code(c) = DistUInt{3}(c - 'a')
    random_char() = uniform(DistUInt{3}, 0, 5)
    deleted = [flip(0.01) for _ in 1:n]
    replaced = [flip(0.01) for _ in 1:n]
    replacement = [random_char() for _ in 1:n]
    ends = [flip(0.99) for _ in 1:n+1, _ in 1:m+1]
    inserted = [random_char() for _ in 1:n+1, _ in 1:m]
    any_of(xs) = reduce(|, xs; init = false)
    memo_ins = Dict{Tuple{Int, Int, Int}, AnyBool}()
    function inserts(k, i, j)
        haskey(memo_ins, (k, i, j)) && return memo_ins[(k, i, j)]
        g = if i == j
            ends[k, i]
        elseif i > m || j < i
            false
        else
            !ends[k, i] & prob_equals(inserted[k, i], code(output[i])) & inserts(k, i + 1, j)
        end
        memo_ins[(k, i, j)] = g
    end
    written(k, d) = (!replaced[k] & (input[k] == d)) | (replaced[k] & prob_equals(replacement[k], code(d)))
    memo = Dict{Tuple{Int, Int}, AnyBool}()
    function perturbs(k, i)
        haskey(memo, (k, i)) && return memo[(k, i)]
        g = if k == n + 1
            inserts(k, i, m + 1)
        else
            kept = any_of([inserts(k, i, j) & written(k, output[j]) & perturbs(k + 1, j + 1) for j in i:m])
            (deleted[k] & perturbs(k + 1, i)) | (!deleted[k] & kept)
        end
        memo[(k, i)] = g
    end
    perturbs(1, 1)
end

model() = @alea begin
    string_editing_perturbs(INPUT, OUTPUT)
end

# hmm.jl of the artifact of Bowers et al., "Stochastic Lazy Knowledge
# Compilation for Inference in Discrete Probabilistic Programs" (PLDI
# 2025), Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.15051140 (CC-BY-4.0), the paper's Table 1,
# row HMM, in the Dice.jl form the artifact gives it as a baseline,
# sequence_models/dice/hmm.jl: the same model, its 50 emissions generated
# and compared with 50 trues. Ported from that file. Mechanical port:
# Dice.List, Dice.Nil and Dice.Cons -> Alea's List, Nil and Cons,
# @dice_ite -> @alea_ite, the add_benchmark! harness dropped, `pr(E)` ->
# E, the query moved to QUERY and model().
using Alea

const QUERY = :pr


function dice_hmm_example(N)

    function make_bool_list(n)
        n == 0 && return Nil(AnyBool)
        Cons(AnyBool, true, make_bool_list(n-1))
    end

    function hmm(z0, num_steps)

        if num_steps == 0
            return Nil(AnyBool)
        end

        z1 = @alea_ite if z0 
            flip(0.7)
        else
            flip(0.1)
        end

        x1 = @alea_ite if z1 
            flip(0.3)
        else
            flip(0.6)
        end

        return Cons(AnyBool, x1, hmm(z1, num_steps - 1))
    end
        
    function bool_lists_equal(l1::List{AnyBool}, l2::List{AnyBool})
        match(l1, [:Nil => () -> match(l2, [:Nil => () -> true, :Cons => (hd, tl) -> false]), :Cons => (x, xs) -> match(l2, [:Cons => (y, ys) -> (@alea_ite if (prob_equals(x, y)); bool_lists_equal(xs, ys); else; false; end), :Nil => () -> false])])
    end 

    return bool_lists_equal(hmm(false, N), make_bool_list(N))
end

model() = dice_hmm_example(50)

function pcfg_defs()

    Pluck.define_type!(:pcfg_grammar_symbol, Dict(:SS => Symbol[], :XX => Symbol[], :YY => Symbol[], :a => Symbol[], :b => Symbol[], :c => Symbol[]))

    @define "generate_pcfg_grammar" """
    (Y (λ generate symbol -> 
      (case symbol of 
        SS => (let (xgen (generate ( XX )) ygen (generate (YY)) order (flip 0.5))
          (if order (append xgen ygen) (append ygen xgen)))
        XX => (if (flip 0.5) (Cons (a) (Nil)) (Cons (b) (append (generate (XX)) (generate (XX)))))
        YY => (Cons (c) (if (flip 0.5) (Nil) (generate (if (flip 0.5) (XX) (SS)))))
      )
    ))
    """

    @define "generate_pcfg_grammar_fuel" """
    (Y (λ generate fuel symbol -> 
      (case fuel of
        S fuel => 
          (case symbol of 
            SS => (let (xgen (generate fuel ( XX )) ygen (generate fuel (YY)) order (flip 0.5))
                (if order (append xgen ygen) (append ygen xgen)))
            XX => (if (flip 0.5) (Cons (a) (Nil)) (Cons (b) (append (generate fuel (XX)) (generate fuel (XX)))))
            YY => (Cons (c) (if (flip 0.5) (Nil) (generate fuel (if (flip 0.5) (XX) (SS)))))
          )
      )
    ))
    """

    @define "symbol_equals" """
    (λ symbol1 symbol2 ->
      (case symbol1 of
        a => (case symbol2 of
          a => true
          b => false
          c => false)
        b => (case symbol2 of
          a => false
          b => true
          c => false)
        c => (case symbol2 of
          a => false
          b => false
          c => true)
      )
    )
    """

    @define "list_symbols_equal" """
    (Y (λ rec list1 list2 ->
      (case list1 of
        Nil => (case list2 of
          Nil => true
          Cons _ _ => false)
        Cons hd1 tl1 => (case list2 of
          Nil => false
          Cons hd2 tl2 => (and (symbol_equals hd1 hd2) (rec tl1 tl2)))
      )
    ))
    """
end

function make_string_from_julia_list(l)
    # l is a list of symbols :a, :b, :c
    # We want to return a string that looks like (Cons (a) (Cons (b) (Cons (c) (Nil))))
    result = ""
    for symbol in l
        result *= "(Cons ($symbol) "
    end
    result *= "(Nil)" * repeat(")", length(l))
    return result
end

function make_long_observation_string(n)
    result_prefix = ""
    result_suffix = ""
    # something of the form abababababab...bcbcbcbcbc with a c in the middle
    for i = 1:n

% defines (perturb_defs, "the one we're using"). The query is the
% probability that perturb turns "edcc" into "eddde":
%   perturb Nil         = random_string 0.99
%   perturb (Cons c cs) = let delete = flip 0.01, insertion = random_string 0.99,
%                             rest = perturb cs
%                         in if delete then rest
%                            else insertion ++ Cons (if flip 0.01 then random_char else c) rest
%   random_string p     = if flip p then Nil else Cons random_char (random_string p)
% with random_char uniform over a to e.

% The perturbation is read against the target left to right: pert(K, I)
% holds where perturb of the input from position K = the target from
% position I to its end, and ins(K, I, J) where the string inserted before
% input position K (K = 4: after the input) is the target's symbols I to
% J - 1. A choice is keyed by the input position it perturbs and, within
% an inserted string, by the target position it writes, which gives the
% original's distribution where no perturbation reads one key twice. The
% input positions are perturbed once each, in order, and an inserted
% string writes each target position once, its end read at the position
% after its last symbol; an empty insertion, or a deleted input
% character, leaves the target position to the next input position, a
% key of its own. No perturbation then reads one key twice, it has the
% original's probability, and the choices at its keys fix it, so that two
% perturbations exclude each other.

input(4).
out(0, e). out(1, d). out(2, d). out(3, d). out(4, e).
target(5).
place(K) :- input(N), between(0, N, K).

0.01::deleted(K) :- in(K, V1).
0.01::replaced(K) :- in(K, V2).
0.2::replacement(K, a); 0.2::replacement(K, b); 0.2::replacement(K, c);

0.99::ends(K, I) :- place(K), target(M), between(0, M, I).
0.2::inserted(K, I, a); 0.2::inserted(K, I, b); 0.2::inserted(K, I, c);
  0.2::inserted(K, I, d); 0.2::inserted(K, I, e) :- place(K), out(I, V4).

ins(K, I, I) :- ends(K, I).
ins(K, I, J) :- out(I, C), \+ends(K, I), inserted(K, I, C), I1 = I + 1, ins(K, I1, J).
written(K, C, C) :- in(K, C), \+replaced(K).
written(K, C, D) :- in(K, C), replaced(K), replacement(K, D).
pert(N, I) :- input(N), target(M), ins(N, I, M).
pert(K, I) :- in(K, V5), deleted(K), K1 = K + 1, pert(K1, I).
